outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no source shows any of the conjectures the bullet can mean being settled; the in-window events are conditional, restricted-case or reduction results (Benoist and Voisin 2024, Watanabe 2024, Park 2024, Kummini and Subramanian 2025, Tipler 2025), plus a January 2026 preprint that generalises Mori's solved ample-tangent-bundle theorem and concerns Kovacs's conjecture rather than a Hartshorne one.
problem_asks: The statement is 'Hartshorne's conjectures' (plural), in the Algebraic geometry section. The frozen January 2024 wikitext gives no link, names no conjecture, states no hypotheses and carries no reference, so the statement alone does not fix which conjectures are meant. The parts the question covers are the status of each conjecture the bullet could refer to. Candidates the literature attaches to Hartshorne, each treated separately below: (A) Hartshorne 1970, Ample subvarieties of algebraic varieties, Ch. III 4.5: if X and Y are submanifolds with ample normal bundles in a projective manifold Z and dim X + dim Y >= dim Z, then X meets Y. (B) Hartshorne 1974, Varieties of small codimension in projective space: a smooth codimension-c subvariety X of P^n is a complete intersection when n is large relative to c, stated variously as n >= 2c+1, c < n/3, n > 3c (Hartshorne's explicit bound as cited by Benoist and Voisin), and in codimension 2 as n >= 2e+1 or n = 4 with e = 2 (as stated by Park). (C) Hartshorne's conjecture on rank-2 bundles: every rank-2 vector bundle on P^n splits into line bundles for n >= 7 (equivalently, no indecomposable rank-2 bundle on P^n for n >= 7; codimension-2 form via the Serre correspondence). (D) Hartshorne's ample-tangent-bundle conjecture (posed in the 1970 notes; the algebraic form of the Frankel conjecture): a smooth projective variety with ample tangent bundle is P^n. (E) Hartshorne's local-algebra conjecture (Conjecture 5.1): for a regular local ring A of dimension n, a prime P with A/P having an isolated singularity, and r = dim A/P > (2n-1)/3, A/P is a complete intersection. (F) Hartshorne's question, as often stated: every irreducible (or connected) curve in P^3 is a set-theoretic complete intersection. (G) Hartshorne's question on cofiniteness of local cohomology modules, which is commutative algebra and sits outside the section. Within each candidate, codimension-2 cases (B, C) and the general case are separate parts. The record does not adopt one reading; each event states which candidate it bears on.

events.what_happened: Benoist and Voisin, 'On the smoothability problem with rational coefficients' (arXiv:2405.12620). They show that a positive answer to the rational Borel-Haefliger smoothing question (Question 0.1: H^{2c}(X,Q)_alg is generated by classes of smooth subvarieties) is incompatible with Conjecture 0.2, Hartshorne's conjecture that a smooth codimension-c subvariety of P^n with n >> c is a complete intersection. Theorem 0.3: the two cannot both have positive answers, even for c = 2. They also prove unconditionally a symplectic variant (Theorem 0.4). Published in Rendiconti Lincei Matematica e Applicazioni 36(3) (2025), 393-408; EMS listing marks it as published online in 2026.
events.revisions: v1 21 May 2024; v2 20 Oct 2024; journal version Rend. Lincei 36(3) 2025 (DOI 10.4171/RLM/1076).
events.delivers: Conditional only. If Question 0.1 has a positive answer then Conjecture 0.2 (candidate B, codimension c, n >> c) fails, and the reverse; the two cannot both hold, even for c = 2 (Theorem 0.3). No counterexample to Conjecture 0.2 is exhibited and Conjecture 0.2 is not proved. The unconditional result (Theorem 0.4) is for compact symplectic manifolds and does not bear on algebraic Conjecture 0.2.
events.remains: Candidate B is neither proved nor refuted, and the paper's own status paragraph says no counterexample to Question 0.1 has been found. Which of Question 0.1 and Conjecture 0.2 fails is left open. Candidates A, C, D, E, F, G are not touched.

events.what_happened: Kiwamu Watanabe, 'Quadratic Varieties of Small Codimension' (arXiv:2405.04002). For a nondegenerate smooth projective X of dimension n in P^{n+c} defined by quadratic equations, Ionescu and Russo had proved candidate B (complete intersection for n >= 2c+1) and classified the extremal case n = 2c. Watanabe classifies the case n = 2c-1 (Theorem 1.2): if X is not a complete intersection it is projectively equivalent to one of the Segre 3-fold P^1 x P^2 in P^5, a hyperplane section of G(2, C^5) in P^9, a hyperplane section of the spinor variety S^10 in P^15, or an 11-dimensional Fano of index 8 in P^17 whose existence the author has not determined.
events.delivers: For quadratically defined X only: the classification of the n = 2c-1 case. That range lies below candidate B's stated range (n >= 2c+1), so the classification does not decide B. The quadratic case of B itself was proved earlier by Ionescu and Russo (2013).
events.remains: Candidate B for smooth X not defined by quadrics; candidate B's stated range is untouched. The existence of the fourth listed variety is open within the paper.

events.direction: Consistent with candidate B: the non-complete-intersection examples it finds have n = 2c-1, outside B's range. No counterexample to B.
events.object: The four varieties of Theorem 1.2, each a non-complete-intersection quadratic X with n = 2c-1: the Segre 3-fold P^1 x P^2 in P^5; a hyperplane section of G(2,5) in P^9; a hyperplane section of the spinor variety S^10 in P^15; and an 11-dimensional Fano variety of index 8 in P^17 whose existence the author has not determined. All are explicit and classified by hand.

events.what_happened: Jinhyung Park, 'Some remarks on smooth projective varieties of small degree and codimension' (arXiv:2405.11933). Gives a short proof of a Ballico-Chiantini theorem: a smooth Fano or Calabi-Yau variety of codimension 2 in P^{n+2} is a complete intersection (abstract: dimension at least 4). Theorem 1.2: assume n >= 2e+1; if d <= cuberoot((n+e^2-2e+2)^2/2)+2 then X in P^r is a complete intersection, improving the Barth-Van de Ven degree bound from about 0.63 n^(1/2) to about 0.79 n^(2/3). Park states the conjecture as: if n >= 2e+1 or n = 4 and e = 2, X is a complete intersection, and adds that it is 'widely open even when e=2 or X is a Fano variety'.
events.revisions: v1 only, 20 May 2024, per arXiv abstract page. Search snippets link the paper to Mathematische Zeitschrift, DOI 10.1007/s00209-026-03965-1; I could not open that page, so the journal link is unverified.
events.delivers: Restricted cases of candidate B. (i) The codimension-2 case with X Fano or Calabi-Yau is settled (a special case of B with e = 2). (ii) For n >= 2e+1, every smooth X of degree d below the Theorem 1.2 bound is a complete intersection, which is B restricted to low degree. Not B in general.
events.remains: Candidate B for codimension 2 with X neither Fano nor Calabi-Yau; candidate B for n >= 2e+1 with degree above the bound; the case n = 4, e = 2 in full generality.
events.time_since_posted: about 28 months since v1; no independent write-up found
events.direction: Consistent with candidate B; proves complete intersection in the restricted regimes listed. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Manoj Kummini and Abhiram Subramanian (Chennai Mathematical Institute), 'On codimension-two subcanonical varieties inside P^n' (arXiv:2511.19962). For a codimension-2 subcanonical local complete intersection X in P^n, under the hypothesis that the ideal sheaf has a nonzero section in a twist j <= (a_X + n + 2)/2, they give sufficient conditions on the first deficiency module H^1_*(I_X) forcing X to be a complete intersection (Theorem 1.1). They also show smooth codimension-2 3-Buchsbaum varieties in P^n, n >= 6, are complete intersections. They cite Ellia's characteristic-0 conjecture for subcanonical codimension-2 varieties with n >= 5.
events.revisions: v1 25 Nov 2025; v2 (HTML body read); v3 26 Aug 2026.
events.delivers: Partial, restricted to codimension-2 subcanonical local complete intersections satisfying the twist hypothesis, plus the smooth 3-Buchsbaum case for n >= 6. This is a special class within candidate B's codimension-2 case and within Ellia's conjecture. Not a general statement.
events.remains: Ellia's characteristic-0 conjecture for all smooth subcanonical codimension-2 X in P^n, n >= 5; candidate B for codimension c >= 3 and for non-subcanonical cases.
events.time_since_posted: about 10.5 months since v1; no independent write-up found
events.doubts: Hypothesis range differs between the sources I read: the arXiv abstract page gives n >= 3 for the codimension-2 statement, while the v2 body states n >= 4 in the introduction and uses n >= 3 in Proposition 2.1. I did not resolve which hypothesis governs the main theorem.
events.direction: Partial positive result in a restricted codimension-2 class. No counterexample, and no claim that Ellia's conjecture is false.

events.what_happened: Carl Tipler, 'Stable toric sheaves. I: Chern classes' (arXiv:2510.14651). Reduces candidate C in the semistable case, Hartshorne's conjecture on indecomposable rank-2 bundles on P^n, to the non-existence of smoothable rank-2 semistable torus-equivariant (toric) torsion-free sheaves on P^n. Gives a formula for Chern classes of reflexive rank-2 toric sheaves, an iterative construction for the general torsion-free case, examples on P^4 and P^5, and existence on P^n for all n >= 3 with prescribed Chern classes satisfying known constraints. A seminar listing dates a talk on the subject to 19 March 2026; the mathematics is dated to the arXiv version.
events.delivers: A reduction of the semistable case of candidate C to a non-existence statement about toric sheaves, plus existence results for toric sheaves. It establishes no non-existence of indecomposable rank-2 bundles on P^n for n >= 7.
events.remains: Candidate C for n >= 7 in full: the reduced non-existence statement and the non-semistable case are both open per the abstract.

events.what_happened: Soham Ghosh, 'Kovacs' conjecture on characterization of projective space and hyperquadrics' (arXiv:2601.10055). Proves that if the p-th exterior power of the tangent bundle of a smooth complex projective variety contains the p-th exterior power of an ample vector bundle, the variety is P^n or a p-dimensional quadric; also a symmetric-power version. The abstract says it gives a common generalisation of Mori, Wahl, Cho-Sato, Andreatta-Wisniewski, Kobayashi-Ochiai and Araujo-Druel-Kovacs characterizations. Not a Hartshorne conjecture.
events.revisions: v1 15 Jan 2026; v2 29 Jan 2026 (adds the symmetric-power version).
events.delivers: Concerns Kovacs's conjecture, a generalisation of the Mori-type characterisation of P^n by ample tangent bundle. It bears on candidate D only as a neighbouring statement, since D itself was settled by Mori in 1979.
events.remains: Not applicable to candidate D, which is already settled. Nothing in the abstract concerns candidates A, B, C, E, F or G.
events.time_since_posted: about 9 months since v1; no independent write-up found
events.direction: Consistent with candidate D (the Mori-type characterisation). It is a generalisation, not a statement about the Hartshorne ample-tangent-bundle conjecture.

events.what_happened: Daniel Erman, Steven Sam and Andrew Snowden, 'Strength and Hartshorne's Conjecture in high degree' (arXiv:1804.09730). Proves candidate B in the regime where the ambient dimension n is much larger than the degree of X: there is a function N(c,e) such that an equidimensional projective subscheme of codimension c and degree e whose singular locus has codimension at least N(c,e) is a complete intersection. The result is field-independent and ineffective. Earlier, Hartshorne proved the characteristic-zero case and Barth-Van de Ven gave an effective bound in characteristic zero.
events.delivers: Candidate B in the regime n >> deg X, in every characteristic, with N(c,e) not effective. Restricted to large n relative to degree.
events.remains: Candidate B for n not large relative to the degree, and in the effective form in positive characteristic.

events.what_happened: Paltin Ionescu and Francesco Russo, 'Manifolds covered by lines and the Hartshorne Conjecture for quadratic manifolds' (arXiv:1209.2047). Prove candidate B for smooth manifolds defined by quadratic equations and list the extremal Hartshorne manifolds (n = 2c). The abstract says small-codimension manifolds defined by equations of small degree are Fano and covered by lines, and are complete intersections exactly when the variety of lines through a general point is so.

events.what_happened: E. Ballico and L. Chiantini, 'On smooth subcanonical varieties of codimension 2 in P^n, n >= 4', Annali di Matematica Pura ed Applicata (1983). As reported by Park (arXiv:2405.11933, Theorem 1.1, citing Ballico-Chiantini Theorem 6): if X is a Fano or Calabi-Yau variety in codimension 2 then X in P^{n+2} is a complete intersection; if d <= 2n+2 likewise. The argument uses a result of Ran. I did not open the 1983 paper; this is taken from Park's statement.

events.what_happened: Shigefumi Mori, 'Projective manifolds with ample tangent bundles', Annals of Mathematics 110 (1979), 593-606. Proves the algebraic form of the Frankel conjecture, which the Wikipedia Frankel article calls the Hartshorne conjecture after Robin Hartshorne: a smooth projective variety with ample tangent bundle is isomorphic to projective space. Mori's proof is in characteristic p as well. Siu and Yau gave an analytic proof over C in 1980.
events.delivers: Full resolution of candidate D (the ample-tangent-bundle conjecture), over an algebraically closed field of any characteristic, as the Frankel Wikipedia article states.

events.what_happened: Thomas Peternell, 'Submanifolds with ample normal bundles and a conjecture of Hartshorne' (arXiv:0804.1023). States candidate A as in Hartshorne 1970 Ch. III 4.5 (cited by Peternell; not checked in the book): if dim X + dim Y >= dim Z then X meets Y. Says the conjecture is 'in principle wide open'. Shows it holds generically, by relating it to the points through which cycles move in covering families, and verifies it in various cases (Theorem 1.2: X meets VG_{m-1}(Z) when N_Y is Griffiths-positive suffices). Section 2 cites a P^2-bundle over a smooth projective surface case.
events.revisions: v1 7 Apr 2008; no journal reference on the arXiv page.
events.delivers: Candidate A only in special or generic situations (the generic case, under Griffiths-positivity hypotheses, and some ambient varieties). Not the general statement.
events.remains: Candidate A in general: X and Y with ample normal bundles in a projective manifold Z with dim X + dim Y >= dim Z meet.
events.direction: Partial support for candidate A. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Robin Hartshorne and Claudia Polini, 'Quasi-cyclic modules and coregular sequences' (arXiv:1907.05472), published Math. Z. 299 (2021), 123-138 per search snippets. For curves in P^3 they give necessary conditions for being a set-theoretic complete intersection. The abstract says an example failing any of these conditions would answer the still-open question whether every connected curve in P^3 is a set-theoretic complete intersection. The abstract does not call this Hartshorne's conjecture.
events.revisions: v1 11 Jul 2019; journal version per search snippets, not opened.
events.delivers: Necessary conditions only, for candidate F. Does not decide whether every curve in P^3 is a set-theoretic complete intersection.
events.direction: No decision for candidate F.

events.what_happened: David Stapleton, 'A noncombinatorial proof that toric rank 2 bundles on projective space split' (arXiv:2001.11075). Abstract frames Hartshorne's conjecture as: rank-2 bundles on n-dimensional projective space split for n at least 7. Proves that torus-equivariant rank-2 bundles on projective space split, re-proving Klyachko's result by a direct, non-combinatorial route, and noting Ilten and Suss's extension to smaller-rank torus actions.
events.revisions: v1 29 Jan 2020; no journal reference on the arXiv page.
events.delivers: Candidate C only in the torus-equivariant case. The general case is not addressed.
events.remains: Candidate C in general (non-equivariant rank-2 bundles on P^n, n >= 7).
events.direction: Partial support for candidate C, in the equivariant case only.

events.what_happened: C. Folegatti, 'On a special class of smooth codimension two subvarieties in P^n, n >= 5' (arXiv:math/0311038). Proves that smooth codimension-2 subcanonical subvarieties of P^n, n >= 5, lying on a hypersurface of degree s that is singular, with multiplicity s-2, along a linear subspace of dimension n-2, are complete intersections. Presented as evidence for Hartshorne's codimension-2 conjecture (Ellia's characteristic-0 form).
events.revisions: v1 4 Nov 2003; no journal reference on the arXiv page.
events.delivers: Restricted codimension-2 subcanonical class, lying on a hypersurface with a prescribed singular linear subspace, n >= 5. A special case within candidate B's codimension-2 instance.
events.remains: Candidate B's codimension-2 instance for subcanonical X outside this class.
events.direction: Consistent with candidate B's codimension-2 instance; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Philippe Ellia and Davide Franco, 'On codimension two subvarieties of P^6' (arXiv:math/9909137); published as 'On codimension two subvarieties of P^5 and P^6', J. Algebraic Geom. 11 (2002). The arXiv abstract states: a smooth codimension-2 subvariety of P^6 lying on a hyperquintic, or of degree less than 74, is a complete intersection; for a smooth subcanonical threefold in P^5 lying on a hyperquartic, it is a complete intersection. The JAG version, as reported by search snippets, states h^0(I_X(5)) not 0 or deg <= 73.
events.revisions: v1 23 Sep 1999 (only version on arXiv); JAG 11 (2002) per search snippet.

events.direction: Consistent with candidate B's codimension-2 instance; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Johan de Jong, blog post 'Hartshorne on local algebra' (Stacks Project blog, 11 January 2019). Quotes Hartshorne's Conjecture 5.1 for a regular local ring A of dimension n with a prime P such that A/P has an isolated singularity: if r = dim A/P > (2n-1)/3 then A/P is a complete intersection. Reports that Tango constructed a nonsplit rank-2 bundle on P^5 in characteristic 2; a general section of a high twist gives a smooth codimension-2 non-complete-intersection subvariety, and pulling back to punctured affine 6-space gives a counterexample at n = 6, r = 4. Says the corrected conjecture uses r > (2n+1)/3, which Tango's example does not refute.
events.delivers: Counterexample to candidate E as originally stated (r > (2n-1)/3), at n = 6, r = 4, in characteristic 2, via Tango's bundle. Does not refute the corrected statement with (2n+1)/3.
events.remains: Candidate E in its corrected form (r > (2n+1)/3). The blog does not resolve it.

events.object: Tango's nonsplit rank-2 vector bundle on P^5 in characteristic 2, which exists only in that characteristic. A general section of a high twist gives a smooth codimension-2 subvariety of P^5 that is not a complete intersection; pulling back to punctured affine 6-space gives a regular local ring A of dimension 6 with a prime P such that A/P has an isolated singularity, has dimension 4, and is not a complete intersection. The non-complete-intersection subvariety comes from a general-section argument, so it is an existence argument rather than an explicit equation; the bundle itself is explicit.

Answers new positive cases of the generalized version of Hartshorne's question on cofiniteness of local cohomology modules, and so of Huneke's conjecture on associated primes. Commutative algebra, not algebraic geometry, and called a question rather than a conjecture in the abstract.

events.what_happened: One manuscript, 'The Campana–Peternell conjecture in dimension six' (OpenAI, dated 25 September 2026), claims that every smooth connected complex projective Fano sixfold with nef tangent bundle is rational homogeneous (Theorem thm:main, proved in sections/07-conclusion.tex). The route: if the Picard number is at least 2, Kanemitsu's theorem for ρ > n−5 applies. If ρ = 1, the minimal-rational-curve analysis leaves P^6, Q^6, pseudoindex 4 and pseudoindex 5; P^6 and Q^6 are homogeneous. Pseudoindex 4 is settled by an intersection-theoretic argument that rules out Kanemitsu's factorization case (a quadric-bundle contradiction). Pseudoindex 5 is the new step: for a general evaluation fibre F (a threefold) with polarization L, the paper derives u = c1(T_F)·L²/L³ satisfying 32−20u+3u² = 0, using characteristic-number identities and a finite linear-algebra calculation. The sectional-genus formula then forces u = 8/3 and L³ = 3, the variety of minimal rational tangents is the Segre P^1×P^2 in P^5, and Mok's recognition theorem gives Gr(2,5). The same manuscript also proves a compact Kähler corollary (cor:nef-tangent-uniformization): a connected compact Kähler X with analytically nef tangent bundle and dim X − q̃(X) ≤ 6 has ordinary universal cover F×C^q̃(X) with F rational homogeneous. It also states a positive Kähler–Einstein metric for Fano manifolds of dimension at most six with nef tangent bundle (cor:positive-ke). Against the candidates in problem_asks: the manuscript never mentions Hartshorne. The only candidate it bears on is (D), the ample-tangent-bundle conjecture (a smooth projective variety with ample tangent bundle is P^n). The introduction cites Mori 1979 for that ample case and calls the nef question 'natural' from it; it does not restate, prove or extend (D) as such. It makes no claim about (A), (B), (C), (E), (F) or (G).
events.delivers: For candidate (D), only the dimension-six special case of the nef question: the theorem gives rational homogeneity for Fano sixfolds with nef tangent bundle. An ample tangent bundle is nef, so a Fano sixfold with ample tangent bundle falls under the theorem; the text does not draw this consequence, does not show that ampleness of T_X forces the Fano property, and does not identify the homogeneous conclusion with P^6 in the ample case. The manuscript does not say it settles Hartshorne's conjectures or any of the candidates, and its own framing is the Campana–Peternell conjecture, which it states as: every smooth complex Fano variety with nef tangent bundle is rational homogeneous. It proves that statement for dimension six only, with the Picard-number-one reduction and the pseudoindex-5 Grassmannian identification as the substantive content. For the Kähler corollary, the claim is the universal-cover splitting F×C^q̃ for dim X − q̃(X) ≤ 6 only.
events.remains: If the claim holds, the Campana–Peternell conjecture remains open in dimensions seven and above, and the compact Kähler uniformization remains open when dim X − q̃(X) ≥ 7. For candidate (D), the text adds nothing beyond the dimension-six nef case and draws no consequence for the ample case in other dimensions. Candidates (A), (B), (C), (E), (F) and (G) are untouched.
events.doubts: (1) The pseudoindex-five identity is established by modular rank computations (mod 10007) and an exact check of six rational columns (sections/05-arithmetic.tex). The text says the certifying program is run as verification/verify.py (sections/08-certificate.tex). The reading here relies on that program, which was not read. (2) The Kähler corollary asserts, in one sentence without its own citation, that every positive-dimensional Albanese fibre is a smooth projective Fano manifold with nef tangent bundle (sections/07-conclusion.tex, lines 81–82). The rest of that proof uses this fact. (3) The text never states a consequence for Hartshorne's ample-tangent-bundle conjecture; the link to candidate (D) exists only through the introduction's citation of Mori 1979 and the nef/ample relation.; conditional on: No hypothesis is assumed. The proof uses published results as black boxes: Kanemitsu 2016 Theorem 0.2 (ρ > n−5); Kanemitsu 2017 (minimal-family proposition, Theorem 3.3, Proposition 4.1, Remarks 2.3 and 4.2) for pseudoindex four and the fibre list; Dedieu–Höring 2017 Theorem 1.3 (pseudoindex at least 6); Mok 2008 Theorem 15 and Hwang–Mok 1999 Propositions 1.2.1–1.2.2 (minimal rational tangents); Kebekus 2002 Theorems 3.3–3.4; Mok's recognition theorem (Mok2008Recognition); and Eisenbud–Green–Hulek–Popescu 2006 Theorem 0.1 (varieties of minimal degree). The pseudoindex-five numerical identity 32−20u+3u² = 0 rests on a finite calculation that the text says is verified by a program, verification/verify.py. That file lies outside build/ and was not read here. The Kähler corollary also depends on Demailly–Peternell–Schneider 1994 (Propositions 3.4 and 3.9, Theorem 3.14), Claudon–Höring–Kollár 2013 Theorem 4.4, Fischer–Grauert 1965, Poczobut 2025 Theorem 1.1, and Bien–Brion 1996.
events.direction: proves a case: the Campana–Peternell conjecture in dimension six (Fano, nef tangent bundle); for candidate (D) only its dimension-six special case

disputes.summary: The statement names no conjecture, and the literature has several conjectures attributed to Hartshorne (candidates A to G in problem_asks). The live Wikipedia footnote points to Barlet-Peternell-Schneider 1990, 'On two conjectures of Hartshorne's', whose content I could not read. This record does not choose a referent.

Frankel conjecture article calls the algebraic ample-tangent-bundle statement the Hartshorne conjecture; Peternell and others use the same name for the ample-normal-bundle intersection statement; Benoist-Voisin and Park use it for the codimension-c complete-intersection statement. These are different statements under one name.

summary: The bullet 'Hartshorne's conjectures' is unlinked in the frozen January 2024 wikitext, which contains no reference tags at all, so I cannot tell from the frozen source which conjecture or citation it carried; the live page attaches a footnote to Barlet-Peternell-Schneider 1990 'On two conjectures of Hartshorne's', which I could not read, so the referent stays open and I recorded each candidate separately. Measured against candidate B (complete intersection for codimension c in P^n with n large relative to c, the most common meaning of 'Hartshorne's conjecture' in recent work), the 2024-2026 in-window events are all partial: Benoist and Voisin (arXiv May 2024, Rend. Lincei) show a positive answer to a rational smoothing question would be incompatible with B, but do not refute B; Watanabe (arXiv May 2024, SIGMA 2025) classifies the n = 2c-1 quadratic non-complete-intersection cases, which lie below B's range; Park (arXiv May 2024) gives a short proof of the Fano and Calabi-Yau codimension-2 case and a degree-restricted case of B; Kummini and Subramanian (arXiv Nov 2025) give criteria for codimension-2 subcanonical varieties. Candidate C (rank-2 bundles on P^n, n >= 7) has one in-window reduction, Tipler (arXiv Oct 2025), which reduces the semistable case to a non-existence statement about toric sheaves. Candidate D was settled by Mori in 1979; Ghosh (arXiv January 2026) generalises Mori's theorem, but to Kovacs's conjecture, so it does not move D. Candidate A has only pre-window partial results (Peternell 2008). Candidate E has a pre-window counterexample to the originally stated bound, at n = 6, r = 4 in characteristic 2 (de Jong's 2019 blog on Tango's bundle), with the corrected bound not refuted. Candidates F and G have only pre-window partial results. Close calls: Benoist-Voisin is conditional, and whether its tension counts as a move against B depends on an open question. Park's degree-bounded result is a restricted case of B, not B. Kummini and Subramanian's hypothesis range differs between their arXiv abstract (n >= 3) and their v2 body (n >= 4 in the introduction). No AI system is named in any Hartshorne-specific source I read; the AI-related items the searches returned concern Batyrev's stringy Hodge conjecture (ChatGPT-assisted counterexample), the generalized Lax conjecture, the Jacobian conjecture, Erdos problems, Fermat's Last Theorem formalisation, the percolation conjecture and AlphaEvolve, none of which is a Hartshorne conjecture. Sra's 'GPT, the Counterexample Machine' (arXiv August 2026) was opened and does not mention Hartshorne. Acknowledgements were read for the in-window papers; for the pre-window papers I did not read every acknowledgements section, so their ai.none_found values rest on the general AI searches and the parts I read.
competing_reading: Read the bullet as candidate D (the ample-tangent-bundle statement, which Wikipedia's Frankel article calls Hartshorne's conjecture): then it was settled by Mori in 1979, before the window, and nothing in the window bears on it except the Ghosh generalisation. Read it as the bullet's own footnote suggests (the two conjectures of Barlet-Peternell-Schneider): then the status depends on content I could not read, and the in-window events may not touch it at all. Read the Benoist-Voisin dichotomy as evidence against candidate B: that would need a positive answer to the rational smoothing question, which no source reports; the dichotomy is conditional, and the paper says no counterexample to Question 0.1 has been found.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The Wikipedia edit history of the bullet and its footnote, to see which conjectures were meant, and whether a citation was present in the January 2024 revision (the repo's frozen wikitext has no reference tags, so it cannot answer this). (2) Reading Barlet-Peternell-Schneider 1990 (Math. Ann. 286, 13-25) to find the two conjectures and what was proved. (3) Hartshorne 1970 (LNM 156) Ch. III 4.5 and the 1974 Bulletin AMS article 'Varieties of small codimension in projective space' for the exact statements; both were not readable here. (4) The Mathematische Zeitschrift version of Park (DOI 10.1007/s00209-026-03965-1) to confirm the journal, date and any changes to the statement. (5) A search of arXiv math.AG for 2026 papers citing Benoist-Voisin or Park, to see whether anyone has discussed the rational smoothing question or extended the Fano and Calabi-Yau case. (6) Tipler's Part II, if posted, for candidate C.

event.what_happened: Jinhyung Park, 'Some remarks on smooth projective varieties of small degree and codimension' (arXiv:2405.11933). Gives a short proof of a Ballico-Chiantini theorem: a smooth Fano or Calabi-Yau variety of codimension 2 in P^{n+2} is a complete intersection (abstract: dimension at least 4). Theorem 1.2: assume n >= 2e+1; if d <= cuberoot((n+e^2-2e+2)^2/2)+2 then X in P^r is a complete intersection, improving the Barth-Van de Ven degree bound from about 0.63 n^(1/2) to about 0.79 n^(2/3). Park states the conjecture as: if n >= 2e+1 or n = 4 and e = 2, X is a complete intersection, and adds that it is 'widely open even when e=2 or X is a Fano variety'.
event.revisions: v1 only, 20 May 2024, per arXiv abstract page. Search snippets link the paper to Mathematische Zeitschrift, DOI 10.1007/s00209-026-03965-1; I could not open that page, so the journal link is unverified.
event.delivers: Restricted cases of candidate B. (i) The codimension-2 case with X Fano or Calabi-Yau is settled (a special case of B with e = 2). (ii) For n >= 2e+1, every smooth X of degree d below the Theorem 1.2 bound is a complete intersection, which is B restricted to low degree. Not B in general.
event.remains: Candidate B for codimension 2 with X neither Fano nor Calabi-Yau; candidate B for n >= 2e+1 with degree above the bound; the case n = 4, e = 2 in full generality.
event.time_since_posted: about 28 months since v1; no independent write-up found
event.direction: Consistent with candidate B; proves complete intersection in the restricted regimes listed. No counterexample.

events.ai_basis: The vast majority of results were obtained with the same procedure using an unreleased internal OpenAI model.

judgement.why: The statement names no conjecture, so I read it as covering the several conjectures attributed to Hartshorne. Any result on one of them, or on a restriction of one, is therefore at most a case. After the snapshot, Park (a new degree-bounded range of the complete-intersection conjecture B) and Kummini–Subramanian (a restricted codimension-2 subcanonical class) are cases. Neither is reviewed, and the journal link for Park is unverified. Benoist–Voisin is a conditional incompatibility and Tipler a reduction; both are none. Watanabe works below B's range, Ghosh proves Kovács's conjecture, and Dosea et al. treat a generalised cofiniteness question; all three are variants. The OpenAI manuscript proves the Campana–Peternell conjecture in dimension six. That is a different conjecture, the manuscript never mentions Hartshorne, and the only bearing it could have, on the ample-tangent-bundle statement, is through a result Mori settled in 1979. I scored it variant. By its README the model generated the work, so its AI role is generated. Before the snapshot, Mori settles candidate D only, so it is a case, not the whole, of a plural statement. De Jong's blog post is a counterexample to E as originally stated: a case, refuted. That post counts as digested because a named expert worked through it publicly.
judgement.doubts: The referent of the bullet cannot be determined: the frozen wikitext has no link or reference, and the paper cited in the live footnote (Barlet–Peternell–Schneider) was not read. If the bullet means only candidate D, Mori 1979 would make the problem resolved before the snapshot. Park's part (i) is a reproof of Ballico–Chiantini; only its degree-bounded theorem is new. The journal acceptances recorded for Ellia–Franco and for Park come from search snippets, so I scored both unreviewed.
